title: Avoid gauges, whose angle is harder to read than a bar’s length.
rule: Leave dials, speedometers and other gauges out of every Oath & Action piece. Draw the same value as a progress bar toward its threshold, or as a bullet graph where a target and ranges matter, so it is read as a length from zero.
use_when: Never: a reader who asks how close a measure is to a mark gets a truer answer from a progress bar or a bullet graph.

use_instead.when: The value is a count toward a threshold
The value sits against a target and ranges

text: A gauge asks the reader to judge an angle on a curved scale, which they do less exactly than a length on a straight one. Its needle, face and color zones take room and ink that a bar spends on the value.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No form: the kit draws no gauge. The sketch, work/build/guide/specimens/s-14-91-sketch.html, draws a gauge beside a progress bar of the same values; build the better choice with progress-bar or bullet-graph.
sketch_alt: A gauge sets an illustrative 70 of 100 as a needle’s angle on a dial, and a progress bar of the same values shows it as a length a reader can measure against the mark at 80. The bar needs no dial to read.
